solution: Squaring \(\sqrt{1+(y')^2}=(y'')^{3/2}\) gives \(1+(y')^2=(y'')^3\). Highest derivative is \(y''\) so order \(=2\); its power is \(3\) so degree \(=3\). Hence \((2,3)\).
\(y\dfrac{dy}{dx}+x=0\Rightarrow y\,dy=-x\,dx\Rightarrow \dfrac{y^2}{2}=-\dfrac{x^2}{2}+c\Rightarrow x^2+y^2=k\), a family of circles.

The stored stem prints \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y+\sqrt{x^2-y^2}}{2}\), but \(/2\) is a source typo for \(/x\) (homogeneous). With \(/x\), put \(y=vx\): \(v+xv'=v+\sqrt{1-v^2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1-v^2}}=\dfrac{dx}{x}\Rightarrow \sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)=\log|x|+c\).
Linear: \(y'+y=\cos x-\sin x\), IF \(=e^x\). \((ye^x)'=e^x(\cos x-\sin x)\); since \(\int e^x(\cos x-\sin x)dx=e^x\cos x\), we get \(ye^x=e^x\cos x+c\).

\(x y'+2y=x^2\log x\Rightarrow y'+\dfrac{2}{x}y=x\log x\). IF \(=e^{\int (2/x)dx}=e^{2\log x}=x^2\). Option (C) \(\tfrac{1}{n^2}\) is a garbled non-answer; the integrating factor is unambiguously \(x^2\).
\(y'=\sec x-y\tan x\Rightarrow y'+y\tan x=\sec x\). IF \(=e^{\int \tan x\,dx}=\sec x\). \((y\sec x)'=\sec^2 x\Rightarrow y\sec x=\tan x+c\).

Eliminating \(a,b\) from \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\): \(\dfrac{x}{a^2}=\dfrac{yy'}{b^2}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{a^2}=\dfrac{(y')^2+yy''}{b^2}\); equating gives \(xy\,y''+x(y')^2-y\,y'=0\) (verified: substitution yields exactly 0). No option matches this — option (B) prints \(2(y')^2\) where the coefficient must be \(x\); B is the intended answer under a \(x\to 2\) typo, but strictly none is correct.

Newton's law: \(T-20=(T_0-20)e^{-kt}\). At \(t=5\): \(50=60\,e^{-5k}\Rightarrow e^{-5k}=\dfrac{5}{6}\). At \(t=15\): \(T-20=60\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^3=60\cdot\dfrac{125}{216}=34.72\Rightarrow T\approx 54.7^{\circ}\)C.
